item.title: Formula One world champion Alan Jones dies after 'short illness'
item.description: Alan Jones , the 1980 Formula One world champion, died on Thursday, only a few days after his 80th birthday. He remains the last Australian to win the F1 title and was only the second Australian to win the championship after Sir Jack Brabham. “We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness,” his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said. “He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for. “Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way. “Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe. “As a family, we would like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who was part of Alan’s journey for the many years of friendship, love and support. He was incredibly fortunate to have so many wonderful people around him.” Alan Jones, Stirling Moss, and Jack Brabham (AP) Born in Melbourne, the son of a racing driver, Jones headed to Europe to further his ambitions and made his Formula One debut in a Hesketh at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix . He took the first of his 12 race wins in Austria for the Shadow team in 1977, but his career was largely undistinguished until he joined Williams in 1978. Jones won five world championship races in the 1980 season and finished on the podium in all but one of the races he completed to clinch the title ahead of Brazilian Nelson Piquet. After an unsuccessful title defence in 1981, he headed back to Australia and bought a farm. Homesickness and a dislike for the British weather played a part. Still, Jones was soon bored of his new life as a cattle breeder and made a one-off F1 comeback in 1983 with Arrows before returning with Haas. The car wasn’t competitive and Jones had a best finish of fourth before leaving F1 again in 1986. Away from F1, Jones won the 1978 Can-Am sportscar title and was third in his only IndyCar race in 1983. Jones kept racing in Australia’s V8 Supercars series until 2002, when he was 55. Jones stayed around the paddock as a TV commentator and race steward but was critical of modern drivers, whom he called “prima donnas” and “too corporate.” Jones is survived by his wife and six children.

item.title: ‘Last one I ever take’ – Joel Embiid vows to stop attempting three-pointers after win over Pistons
item.description: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid will focus his attention on scoring from inside the three-point line after a terrible start to the season as an outside shooter. The 76ers credentials as championship contenders look solid right now, as the roster seems to have already assimilated LeBron James and Jaylen Brown perfectly, picking up a 112-106 win over the No. 2-seeded Detroit Pistons. Embiid was one of the key players in the win, but entirely due to his ability closer to the basket. After going 0-for-3 on three-point attempts in the win, Embiid learned a lesson for the rest of the season. Joel Embiid says he will not attempt more three-pointers Embiid is shooting 11.5% from three this season, going 3-for-36 on the season. After missing three attempts against the Pistons, he let the media know how he feels about taking more long-range shots this season. “My three is just gone for whatever reason. Tonight might’ve been the last three I ever take.” Embiid had one of his best games of the season against Detroit, ending the night with 26 points and 15 rebounds, shooting 8-for-15 on two-point field goal attempts. Embiid is averaging 19.6 points, 10.0 rebounds and 4.4 assists over the season so far, allowing stars like Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown to lead the team offensively while playing his role to perfection. The 76ers will need Embiid to be a floor-spacer to effectively play a style of basketball that maximises the downhill ability of Maxey, Brown, and LeBron. LeBron in particular has shown he can be most lethal as a playmaker when he is coming downhill and opening up passing opportunities. If teams start leaving Embiid unguarded on the three-point line, the 32-year-old center will definitely attempt those open opportunities. Given he has proven pedigree as a shooter, it’s a matter of time before he finds his rhythm again. It’s been a rough shooting season for Embiid through eight games of the season, but it is hard to believe he will completely stop attempting threes. He might be more judicious and wait for wide-open opportunities to get his shot going again, but it’s highly unlikely he stops shooting them altogether. item.title: Valverde’s stoppage-time strike completes Real Madrid comeback at AEK for 12 points from 12
item.description: Valverde’s stoppage-time strike completes Real Madrid comeback at AEK for 12 points from 12 Substitute captain Federico Valverde struck in stoppage time as Real Madrid twice came from behind to beat AEK Athens 3-2. The win keeps Mourinho's side perfect in the league phase and takes them past his qualification target, days before a trip to Valencia without Vinícius. Federico Valverde came off the bench in Athens and settled a match Real Madrid had trailed twice. The captain’s long-range strike arrived in the second minute of stoppage time. It completed another away comeback in this Champions League campaign. Mourinho’s side remain perfect after four matchdays. AEK struck first. Koita put the hosts ahead in the 12th minute. Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside after a review just before the half-hour. He did not have to wait long. In the 32nd minute he equalised with a backheel from Cucurella’s cross. AEK went ahead again with 15 minutes of normal time left. Stavros Pilios ran onto a pass from Koita and shot through Courtois’s legs. Madrid answered in less than three minutes. Denzel Dumfries played a low ball across goal and Mbappé made it 2-2. The night ended badly for Koita. AEK’s opening scorer was sent off at 90+5, after the final whistle. He had kept protesting to the referee despite repeated warnings. Valverde decides the game after a hamstring scare The winner carried extra weight given Valverde’s recent fitness. He felt strong discomfort in his right hamstring in the 23rd minute of the 2-1 Clásico win at Camp Nou. Mourinho said afterwards that Valverde had played more than 40 minutes injured. In Athens he started on the bench, yet still had the final say. Madrid’s European record now reads four wins from four. They beat Inter 2-1 at home, came back to win 4-3 at Roma and beat Leipzig 4-1 at home before this trip. Their tally of 12 points takes them past the 11–12 point mark Mourinho set as the target for qualification. The next aim is a top-eight finish. The pattern is notable. Both the Roma and AEK wins came after Madrid had fallen behind away from home. In Athens they had to respond on two separate occasions. Madrid head to Mestalla still without the suspended Vinícius Attention now turns to LaLiga, where Madrid remain without Vinícius. On 16 October, the RFEF Appeals Committee rejected the club’s appeal and upheld his ban. Two games were for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair against Villarreal. The other two were for confronting the referee afterwards. The suspension covered the league games against Sevilla, Barcelona and Racing. The last of the four matches is at Valencia’s Mestalla on 7 November, three days after the win in Athens. Europe then returns. Madrid host PSV on Tuesday 24 November at 9pm CET. They then travel to Arsenal on Wednesday 9 December. Victor Wembanyama had to put the San Antonio Spurs on his back on Wednesday, as he recorded a career-high 52 points to go along with 24 rebounds and eight blocks to power them to a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks. The Spurs needed every bit of Wembanyama’s contributions, as the entire team simply did not bring it on offense tonight. The Spurs team, outside of Wembanyama made just 21 of their 67 field-goal attempts, which is “good” for a 31.3% clip. But in the end, the team showed up in support of Wembanyama when it mattered. In particular, head coach Mitch Johnson praised De’Aaron Fox for the way he defended Kyrie Irving on the final possession of the game to seal the win for San Antonio — giving his effort an A+ grade , as per Jeff Garcia of Spurs In Focus. However, Fox kept in step with Irving, didn’t give him an inch of space, and was all up in his grill when the Mavericks star shot the ball — forcing the attempt to go wide left. KYRIE IRVING FOR THE WIN 🔥 pic.twitter.com/55gfonhuvX — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 5, 2026 Fox also made some crucial plays in the clutch on offense. There were many who called for the Spurs to try and trade Fox this past offseason after his brutal showing in the 2026 NBA Finals. But his veteran presence helps calm down this squad, and at his best, he provides the Spurs with the kind of downhill burst and defensive effort they need from their floor general. On the season, Fox is averaging 15.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 6.1 assists in eight games. item.title: Meet the people set for key role in deciding Man City fate
item.description: Manchester City have been sponsored by Etihad since May 2009 [Getty Images] They are the five individuals at the Premier League set to play a key role in the fate of Manchester City. The competition's board has the responsibility of recommending a punishment after the seismic news in September of the club being found guilty of breaching financial rules by an independent commission. While that three-person commission panel will ultimately decide on a sanction, the Premier League's submission will be considered, along with the view of City of course, who maintain their innocence and have appealed. It is not known when a sanction hearing will take place, nor what sanction the Premier League will want, with a fine, points deduction, expulsion or the stripping of past titles all possible. But who makes up the Premier League's board, and how have their recommendations over punishments been received in past disciplinary cases? BBC Sport has taken a close look. Among various roles and responsibilities, the board is the entity responsible for prosecuting breaches of Premier League rules. It comprises the league's chair, chief executive, and three independent non-executive directors, with no club representatives included - in order to provide independence and neutrality. Do Manchester City have any grounds to win their appeal? How much did Man City's rule breaking cost your team? The chair Alison Brittain has kept a low profile since becoming the league's first female chair almost four years ago. Formerly a senior executive in the hospitality and financial services sectors, she is also chair and trustee of The King's Trust Group. Described as "sensible" by one acquaintance, in September she spoke at a university alumni event, revealing that she was initially sceptical about joining the Premier League because she had never worked in sport. Two senior club executives - the former Arsenal CEO Vinai Venkatesham (now at Spurs), and ex-Aston Villa CEO Christian Purslow - told her that her skillset was what the league needed, helping to persuade her to apply. She said: "They actually spent some time talking to me and saying 'we aren't looking for a super fan. In fact we're looking for the exact opposite - somebody who will bring a different mindset. A business mindset, governance standards, be able to reset us a little bit into a different way'…and so I then went through the process and ended up in the job." The Dallas Mavericks may have given them a run for their money, but the San Antonio Spurs held strong, thanks in large part to a monster outing from Victor Wembanyama . Wembanyama finished with a bonkers stat line of 52 points (a career-high), 24 rebounds, and eight blocks, leading the way for the Spurs in a 112-111 victory over the Mavericks to move to 6-2 on the season. It looked like the Spurs were on their way to a convincing victory after leading by double digits heading into the second half. But the Mavericks clawed their way back , and the Spurs’ mettle was tested. After all, this was a team that blew multiple fourth-quarter leads in the 2026 NBA Finals and choked away a title because of it. And it looks like Wembanyama’s perspective of his game was shaped by that past experience. The Spurs star expressed some regrets over his performance, particularly with some of his plays late in the game, despite his dominance amid his team’s victory. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I wish I set better screens towards the end and made more free throws,” Wembanyama told ESPN’s Katie George in his postgame interview. He would just make on his last five attempts, which kept the door open for the Mavericks to steal the game in the end. item.title: UConn Women's Basketball: Another Recognition Awaits Azzi Fudd
item.description: Azzi Fudd will join an exclusive club of UConn Huskies on Sunday when she is inducted into the Huskies of Honor. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 1:30 p.m. at Gampel Pavilion, a half-hour ahead of the tipoff of a highly anticipated women’s basketball game between the No. 2 Huskies and No. 10 Iowa Hawkeyes . Fudd will become the 25th player honored on the women’s basketball side of the Huskies of Honor. How Azzi Fudd qualifies For a UConn women’s basketball player to enter the Huskies of Honor, the player must have graduated from UConn and been selected by the Women's Basketball Coaches Association as a first-team All-American. As a senior in the 2025-26 season, Fudd was selected to the WBCA, Associated Press and USBWA All-America first teams. She actually holds two UConn degrees – a bachelor's degree in communication in 2024 and a Master of Business Administration degree in 2026 – to cement her eligibility. Azzi Fudd is UConn's all-time leader at the foul line, shooting 92.5%. Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Fudd’s UConn achievements Fudd filled the trophy shelf with honors she earned as a member of the Huskies, both for her work on the court and in the classroom. Those honors include: 2026 CSC Academic All-America First Team 2026 CSC Academic All-America Team Member of the Year 2026 Big East Scholar-Athlete of the Year 2026 NCAA Fort Worth Regional 1 All-Region Team 2025 NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player 2022 NCAA Tournament Bridgeport All-Region Team Two-time All-Big East First Team and Big East All-Tournament Team selection (2025, 2026) A year after helping the Huskies win the 2025 NCAA championship, Fudd was the No. 1 selection in the 2026 WNBA Draft, chosen by the Dallas Mavericks. Despite her debut season being cut short with 13 games remaining due to a right-knee injury, Fudd earned a spot on the 2026 Associated Press WNBA All-Rookie Team. She averaged 13.1 points, 1.7 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.7 steals per game. Her sharpshooting abilities made her the first rookie to win the WNBA 3-Point Contest over All-Star Weekend. Fudd finished her UConn career with 1,687 points, 270 rebounds, 241 assists and 191 steals. Her 92.5% free throw percentage is No. 1 in UConn history. An academic All-American, Fudd always was eloquent when speaking with the media as a UConn student. Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Other members of Huskies of Honor Fudd will join five Huskies national championship teams, head coach Geno Auriemma and assistant coach Chris Dailey as well as some of the most prolific players in UConn’s storied history in the Huskies of Honor. The list includes Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame members Rebecca Lobo, Sue Bird and Maya Moore, as well as Diana Taurasi, who undoubtedly will join them when eligible. Current WNBA standouts including Napheesa Collier, Breanna Stewart, Gabby Williams, Paige Bueckers and Aaliyah Edwards also are honored at Gampel Pavilion. Edwards was the most recent addition, inducted in January.

item.title: Swap deal involving Barcelona homegrown star and Inter Milan defender was never close – Romano
item.description: Swap deal involving Barcelona homegrown star and Inter Milan defender was never close – Romano Barcelona have been suffering from numerous defensive injuries in recent weeks, forcing Hansi Flick to get creative with his team selection. Among the many names the Catalan club have been linked with is Inter Milan star Federico Dimarco . However, it has emerged that he is close to extending his contract. Alejandro Balde has lost prominence under Hansi Flick this season, and Barça had explored an arrangement to offer the Spaniard in exchange for the Italian back in the summer. However, according to Fabrizio Romano , a swap deal between Balde and Dimarco was neither close nor feasible. Inter have always wanted to retain the Italian international, while Balde himself had no intention of leaving Barcelona last summer. Romano clarifies Balde-Dimarco situation The two left-backs were linked with a potential exchange during the summer transfer window, but the deal never developed. Barcelona had explored the possibility of selling Balde after Hansi Flick lost faith in him, with Manchester United also interested. Dimarco never looked close to joining Barcelona. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) However, Balde decided to stay at the Catalan club and prove his worth to the manager, which hasn’t worked out so far. Had Barcelona sold the 23-year-old, they might have wanted a new left-back in the squad, and Dimarco would have been perfect. However, Romano’s clarification makes it clear that the option was never on the table, and Inter have now activated the Italian’s one-year contract extension . Barcelona face important decisions at left-back For Barcelona, the situation is particularly interesting because Balde’s future remains uncertain. The La Masia graduate has struggled for regular minutes under Hansi Flick, with Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart ahead of him in the pecking order. What does the future hold for Balde at Barcelona? (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) Even with four defenders injured, Hansi Flick has chosen to play Brian Farinas at right-back rather than put Balde in his line-up. Nevertheless, Balde’s desire to remain at Barcelona is an important part of the story. It remains to be seen whether he changes that stance come January. Barcelona would benefit from selling a player Hansi Flick doesn’t count on and using that money to bring in a centre-back, which is a pressing need in the squad. It remains to be seen how Hansi Flick handles this situation and who Barça go for if Balde leaves in the winter transfer window.

item.title: Real Madrid set historic European record after Valverde’s dramatic winner against AEK Athens
item.description: Real Madrid set historic European record after Valverde’s dramatic winner against AEK Athens Real Madrid kept their winning streak intact against AEK Athens, securing a late 3-2 victory to make it seven wins in a row for Jose Mourinho’s team. The Greek side pushed Los Blancos to the limit and took the lead twice, only to see Madrid snatch victory in the dying minutes. Federico Valverde’s dramatic winner against AEK Athens on Wednesday was not only worth three points but also highlighted a historic European record. According to LaLigaenDirecto , Real Madrid have now scored 49 goals in the 90th minute or later in European Cup and Champions League history, more than any other club. The important caveat is that these numbers do not include the goals Los Blancos have scored in extra time. Valverde’s winner adds another chapter to Madrid’s European history The latest addition to the list came in the 92nd minute against AEK Athens, when the captain unleashed a superb long-range strike to make it 3-2 on the night. Valverde scored a stunner against AEK Athens. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) Los Blancos had already pulled level twice in the game through Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe. The result helped Mourinho’s team preserve their perfect Champions League record this season, with four victories in four games. Late goals have played an important role in Los Blancos pulling off a number of heists in European competition in recent years. Even this season, Mourinho’s side left it late against Roma, scoring three goals in the last 10 minutes to turn a 3-1 deficit into a 4-3 victory. The most iconic of these late goals has to be Sergio Ramos’ stoppage-time equaliser against Atletico Madrid in the 2014 Champions League final. Rodrygo’s incredible late double against Manchester City in the 2022 semi-finals is another significant moment. A mentality that transcends generations Real Madrid have achieved a European milestone. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) The best part about this goalscoring record for Real Madrid is that it has remained consistent across managers and generations. Madrid are a side that can never be counted out until the final whistle, no matter how much their backs are against the wall. The sheer resilience, refusal to accept defeat and determination to keep fighting until the very end are why Los Blancos have 15 Champions League titles. Now, in their quest for a 16th, Jose Mourinho’s side are showing similar determination and winning games even when they are on the brink of defeat. The AEK Athens win will further motivate the group to keep performing and keep their winning streak intact. They will hope to round off this excellent period with another three points against Valencia this weekend before the squad disperses for the international break.

item.title: 'We need to step up a little bit' - Erling Haaland urges Manchester City to be more ruthless after scoring late winner in 3-2 Champions League triumph at RB Leipzig
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-LEIPZIG-MAN CITY - AFP Manchester City striker Erling Haaland urged his team-mates to show greater ruthlessness after netting a 78th-minute winner in Wednesday's 3-2 Champions League victory at RB Leipzig. The Premier League visitors twice surrendered their lead in Germany before their captain struck from close range to lift them to seventh in the table. Norwegian talisman demands killer instinct Haaland rescued Enzo Maresca's side after they arrived in Germany following consecutive league defeats and a Carabao Cup shootout win over Brighton. Converting Elliot Anderson's low cross with his 13th touch, the forward took his career tally against the hosts to 13 goals in nine games . However, the match-winner remained frustrated by his team's failure to kill the contest off earlier. Defensive lapses precede decisive intervention City led before half-time through Castello Lukeba's own goal from Nico O'Reilly's cross before Ridle Baku beat Gianluigi Donnarumma at his near post, while Antonio Nusa cancelled out Enzo Fernandez's 57th-minute header just three minutes later. Speaking to TNT Sports afterwards, Haaland said: "The most important is that I helped the team to win, and I managed to do that today, so I'm super happy. "I think in the end, we need to step up a little bit because I think when we were 1-0 up, I think we need to push forward a bit more to go at it, to go for the second and then hopefully go for the third. That's what we have to do as a club, we have to work on that." Asked what City must do differently, he continued: "I think keep the ball, when to keep it, when to go, and working together, both offensively, defensively, loads of different things. "That's a good part, you can always get better, and there's always a new chance in a new game in three days, so that's lovely." Prolific marksman embraces limited touches According to Opta, the striker's haul against Leipzig is his highest against any opponent in Europe's top five leagues. Questioned on his limited touches before scoring, Haaland added: "I mean, you can look at it in a few different ways. "You can look at it that is difficult to keep concentrated for around 100 minutes, or you can look at it in a positive way that it's only 100 minutes that you have to fully focus to hopefully be ready when the chance comes. You can look at it in a few different ways, and I look at it in the second option." Forest trip tests domestic revival Maresca's second-placed side now look to end their two-match domestic losing streak when they visit Nottingham Forest this weekend . Tightening up defensively after shipping soft equalisers in midweek will be essential to keep pace in the title race. Victory at the City Ground would restore momentum before the international break.

Vít Krejčí headed to the Locker Room suffers ankle injury, he will not return #ripcity pic.twitter.com/b6ennMxvtM — DJACK (@DJACK_RipCity) November 5, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Blazers reported that Krejci had suffered an ankle injury, leaving him unable to return for what would be an eventual win against the Suns. But after the game, head coach Micah Nori said that the actual injury that forced an early exit for Krejci was a leg fracture , as per ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel. item.title: Lakers beat Kings behind Luka Dončić’s third straight 40-point game
item.description: Nov 4, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers forward/guard Luka Doncic (77) controls the ball against the Sacramento Kings during the second quarter at Golden 1 Center. SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Luka Dončić scored 11 straight points for the Los Angeles Lakers in the second quarter Wednesday night, then helped finish off the Sacramento Kings at the free-throw line in the fourth. Dončić finished with 40 points, nine rebounds and seven assists as the Lakers beat the Kings 116-103 at Golden 1 Center. It was his third straight 40-point game (and fourth in last five games) and the third straight win for L.A., improving their record to 7-2. Dončić shot 11 of 23 from the field and made six 3-pointers. He has recorded at least 35 points, five rebounds, five assists and five 3-pointers in six consecutive appearances. The rest of the NBA has combined for five such games this season. It was the 66th time Dončić reached those marks in his career, moving him past Stephen Curry for second all time, according to the team. Austin Reaves added 21 points on 7-of-15 shooting, and Walker Kessler finished with 15 points, eight rebounds, four blocks and three steals. The Lakers finished with 13 blocks and 11 steals, converting 18 Sacramento turnovers into 23 points. Sacramento opened with a 16-8 lead, but Dončić scored 10 points in the first quarter and the Lakers pulled even at 28 by the end of the period. L.A. made five 3-pointers in the quarter while scoring just four points in the paint. Dončić’s second-quarter run brought him to 21 points in his first 16 minutes with a flamethrower run where he scored 11 straight points. The Lakers made 10 3-pointers before halftime and turned 11 Sacramento turnovers into 12 points to take a 61-54 lead into the break. The Kings opened the third quarter on a 15-12 run to cut the deficit to four. The Lakers answered by outscoring Sacramento 14-5 the rest of the quarter, building a lead that reached 16 before taking an 87-74 advantage into the fourth. Sacramento cut an 18-point fourth-quarter deficit to seven before Dončić helped close out the win from the line. The Lakers made 15 of 17 free throws in the fourth quarter and finished 34 of 38 for the game. Darius Acuff Jr. led Sacramento with 22 points and 12 assists. Zach LaVine scored 21 points, and Domantas Sabonis added 16 points and 17 rebounds as the Kings fell to 1-7. The Lakers host the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday.
